newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Dec CPI rose 3.20 percent - Banco de Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Dec CPI rose 3.20 percent - Banco de Mexico.

text.p: Mexico's consumer price index rose 3.20 percent in December from the month before after rising 1.52 percent in November, Banco de Mexico said on Thursday.
The central bank said that 1996 inflation ended at 27.70 percent -- in line with expectations although higher than the government's original target of 20.5 percent.
A survey of six economists by Reuters this week forecast a rise of 3.47 percent in December's consumer prices.
The central bank added that the producer price index rose 2.66 percent in December from the month before, compared to a rise of 1.69 percent in November.
Banco de Mexico said the rate of inflation during December would have been 1.05 percentage points lower had there not been increases in gasoline and public transportation prices.

It said that the main causes of inflation besides hikes in gasoline and public transportation prices were an increase in prices of meat, housing, auto parts, restaurants, domestic gas, cigarettes, milk, eggs, and other products.
It said that prices for the basic basket of consumer goods rose 4.84 percent in December from the month before.
For the year, prices for the basic basket of consumer goods rose 33.30 percent.
